title: General Bible
description: Version-one General Bible task pack for The Way: A Journey Through Bible Lands. Authored under CONTENT_AUTHORING.md; grows across PHASE9_SPEC.md's Groups N4-N10.

tasks.title: The Exodus Leader
tasks.prompt: Who led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt?

normalVariant.prompt: Who led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Moses, Aaron, or Joshua?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the leader who led Israel out of Egypt and the brother who spoke for him.

clues: He grew up in Pharaoh's household.
God spoke to him from a burning bush.
tasks.teachingReveal: Moses led Israel out of Egypt after God called him at the burning bush; his brother Aaron served as his spokesman before Pharaoh.

tasks.title: Builder of the Ark
tasks.prompt: Who built a great boat, or ark, at God's command to survive a flood?

normalVariant.prompt: Who built a great boat, or ark, at God's command to survive a flood?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Noah, Abraham, or Lot?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the builder of the ark, and how many days and nights it rained.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Noah, forty days and forty nights
acceptedAnswers: Noah and forty days and nights

clues: He was warned that a flood was coming.
He brought two of every kind of animal aboard.
tasks.teachingReveal: Noah built the ark at God's command and was saved with his family when the flood came, after forty days and nights of rain.

tasks.title: Swallowed by a Great Fish
tasks.prompt: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish after running from God's call?

normalVariant.prompt: Which prophet was swallowed by a great fish after running from God's call?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Jonah, Elijah, or Amos?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the prophet, and the city God had sent him to warn.

clues: He was fleeing by ship in the opposite direction from where God sent him.
He was inside the fish for three days.
tasks.teachingReveal: Jonah tried to flee from God's call to preach to Nineveh, was swallowed by a great fish, and after three days was brought back to dry land to obey.

tasks.title: The First Man
tasks.prompt: According to Genesis, who was the first man God created?

normalVariant.prompt: According to Genesis, who was the first man God created?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Adam, Cain, or Seth?

clues: God formed him from the dust of the ground.
He was placed in the Garden of Eden.
tasks.teachingReveal: Genesis describes God forming Adam from the dust of the ground and placing him in the Garden of Eden.

tasks.title: The First Woman
tasks.prompt: According to Genesis, who was the first woman, formed from the man's rib?

normalVariant.prompt: According to Genesis, who was the first woman, formed from the man's rib?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Eve, Sarah, or Rebekah?

clues: Her name means 'living' or 'life-giver.'
She was Adam's wife in the Garden of Eden.
tasks.teachingReveal: Genesis describes God forming Eve from Adam's rib to be his wife and companion in the Garden of Eden.

tasks.title: David and the Giant
tasks.prompt: Who was the young shepherd who defeated the giant Goliath?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was the young shepherd who defeated the giant Goliath?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it David, Saul, or Jonathan?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the shepherd who defeated Goliath, and the weapon he used.

clues: He later became king of Israel.
He refused King Saul's armor before the fight.
tasks.teachingReveal: David, a young shepherd, defeated the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone, trusting in God rather than armor or weapons.

tasks.title: The Lions' Den
tasks.prompt: Who was thrown into a den of lions for praying to God, and was kept safe overnight?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was thrown into a den of lions for praying to God, and was kept safe overnight?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Daniel, Ezekiel, or Jeremiah?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name who was thrown to the lions, and who kept him safe.
acceptedAnswers: Daniel, an angel shut the lions' mouths

clues: He served as an official in the Babylonian and Persian courts.
He was punished for continuing to pray three times a day.
tasks.teachingReveal: Daniel was thrown into a den of lions for continuing to pray to God despite a royal decree, and God sent an angel to shut the lions' mouths.

tasks.title: The First Day
tasks.prompt: According to Genesis, what did God create on the very first day?

normalVariant.prompt: According to Genesis, what did God create on the very first day?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it light, the sun, or the stars?

clues: God spoke a single command to bring it into being.
God then separated it from the darkness.
tasks.teachingReveal: On the first day of creation, God said 'Let there be light,' and separated the light from the darkness.

tasks.title: The Mother of Jesus
tasks.prompt: Who was the mother of Jesus?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was the mother of Jesus?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Mary, Martha, or Elizabeth?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the mother of Jesus, and the angel who announced His birth to her.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Mary, told by the angel Gabriel

clues: She lived in the town of Nazareth.
An angel told her she would give birth to the Son of God.
tasks.teachingReveal: Mary, a young woman from Nazareth, was told by the angel Gabriel that she would give birth to Jesus, the Son of God.

tasks.title: Six Days of Work
tasks.prompt: According to the Ten Commandments, how many days were the Israelites told they could work each week?

normalVariant.prompt: According to the Ten Commandments, how many days were the Israelites told they could work each week?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it six, five, or seven?

clues: The remaining day of the week was set apart for rest.
This pattern mirrored God's own work in creation.
tasks.teachingReveal: The fourth commandment instructs six days of work followed by a seventh day of rest, mirroring the pattern of creation.

tasks.title: Mary's Husband
tasks.prompt: Who was Mary's husband, and the earthly, adoptive father of Jesus?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was Mary's husband, and the earthly, adoptive father of Jesus?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Joseph, Zechariah, or Simeon?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name Mary's husband, and the trade he worked.

clues: An angel appeared to him in a dream, telling him not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife.
He worked as a carpenter.
tasks.teachingReveal: Joseph, a carpenter engaged to Mary, was told by an angel in a dream not to be afraid to take her as his wife, since the child was conceived by the Holy Spirit.

tasks.title: The Birthplace of Jesus
tasks.prompt: In what town was Jesus born?

normalVariant.prompt: In what town was Jesus born?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Bethlehem, Nazareth, or Jerusalem?

clues: A Roman census required Joseph and Mary to travel there.
This town was also known as the city of David.
tasks.teachingReveal: Jesus was born in Bethlehem, the town of David, after Joseph and Mary traveled there for a Roman census.

tasks.title: Thirty Pieces of Silver
tasks.prompt: Which of Jesus' twelve disciples betrayed Him for thirty pieces of silver?

normalVariant.prompt: Which of Jesus' twelve disciples betrayed Him for thirty pieces of silver?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Judas Iscariot, Thomas, or Simon Peter?

clues: He identified Jesus to the arresting soldiers with a kiss.
He later returned the silver in remorse.
tasks.teachingReveal: Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve disciples, betrayed Jesus to the religious leaders for thirty pieces of silver, identifying Him with a kiss.

tasks.title: The Day of Resurrection
tasks.prompt: According to the Gospels, on which day of the week was Jesus' tomb found empty?
tasks.answer: The first day of the week
acceptedAnswers: The first day of the week

normalVariant.prompt: According to the Gospels, on which day of the week was Jesus' tomb found empty?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it the first day of the week, the sixth day, or the seventh day?
options: The first day of the week

clues: Women came early in the morning to the tomb to anoint the body.
This is the day now widely observed as Easter.
tasks.teachingReveal: The Gospels record that women found the tomb empty early on the first day of the week — the day now widely observed as Easter.

tasks.title: Three Denials
tasks.prompt: Which disciple denied knowing Jesus three times on the night of His arrest?

normalVariant.prompt: Which disciple denied knowing Jesus three times on the night of His arrest?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Peter, John, or Andrew?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the disciple who denied Jesus three times, and the sound that reminded him of Jesus' warning.

clues: Jesus had predicted this would happen before a rooster crowed.
He wept bitterly afterward.
tasks.teachingReveal: Peter denied knowing Jesus three times in a courtyard, just as Jesus had predicted; when the rooster crowed, Peter remembered and wept bitterly.

tasks.title: Crossing the Sea
tasks.prompt: What sea did God part so the Israelites could escape Pharaoh's army on dry ground?

normalVariant.prompt: What sea did God part so the Israelites could escape Pharaoh's army on dry ground?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it the Red Sea, the Dead Sea, or the Sea of Galilee?

clues: Moses stretched out his hand over the water.
The Egyptian army drowned pursuing Israel through it.
tasks.teachingReveal: God parted the Red Sea when Moses stretched out his hand, letting Israel cross on dry ground while the pursuing Egyptian army was drowned.

tasks.title: Strength in His Hair
tasks.prompt: Which judge of Israel had great strength that was tied to a vow never to cut his hair?

normalVariant.prompt: Which judge of Israel had great strength that was tied to a vow never to cut his hair?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Samson, Gideon, or Ehud?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the judge with vowed strength, and who cut his hair to weaken him.

clues: He was a Nazirite from birth, under a vow to God.
A woman named Delilah discovered the secret of his strength.
tasks.teachingReveal: Samson, a judge of Israel under a Nazirite vow never to cut his hair, was betrayed by Delilah, who had his hair cut to strip him of his strength.

tasks.title: Israel's First King
tasks.prompt: Who was anointed as the first king of Israel, before David?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was anointed as the first king of Israel, before David?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Saul, David, or Samuel?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name Israel's first king, and the prophet who anointed him.

clues: He was described as standing head and shoulders above the people.
The prophet Samuel anointed him with oil.
tasks.teachingReveal: Saul was anointed by the prophet Samuel to become Israel's first king, at the people's request for a king like other nations.

tasks.title: The Wisdom of a King
tasks.prompt: Which king of Israel, famous for his wisdom, settled a dispute between two women who both claimed the same baby?

normalVariant.prompt: Which king of Israel, famous for his wisdom, settled a dispute between two women who both claimed the same baby?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Solomon, David, or Rehoboam?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the wise king, and what he asked God for when given the chance to ask for anything.

clues: He was David's son.
He built the great Temple in Jerusalem.
tasks.teachingReveal: Solomon, David's son, asked God for wisdom to govern well, and his wise ruling in the case of the two women became famous throughout Israel.

tasks.title: A Prophet's Rebuke
tasks.prompt: Which prophet confronted King David with a parable about a poor man's lamb, after David's sin with Bathsheba?

normalVariant.prompt: Which prophet confronted King David with a parable about a poor man's lamb, after David's sin with Bathsheba?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Nathan, Gad, or Samuel?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the prophet, and the words he used to accuse David after the parable.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Nathan, who said 'You are the man'

clues: He told a story about a rich man who stole a poor man's only lamb.
He declared, 'You are the man,' directly accusing the king.
tasks.teachingReveal: The prophet Nathan confronted King David with a parable about a poor man's lamb, then declared 'You are the man,' exposing David's sin with Bathsheba.

tasks.title: Three Hundred Men
tasks.prompt: Which judge led just three hundred men to defeat the vast army of Midian?

normalVariant.prompt: Which judge led just three hundred men to defeat the vast army of Midian?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Gideon, Barak, or Othniel?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the judge, and the method God used to narrow his army down to three hundred.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Gideon, narrowed by how the men drank water
acceptedAnswers: Gideon, the way the men drank water

clues: God reduced his army from thousands down to three hundred.
His men carried torches hidden inside clay jars.
tasks.teachingReveal: Gideon led just three hundred men, chosen by how they drank water at a stream, to defeat the vast army of Midian, so that Israel would know the victory was God's.

tasks.title: Sold by His Brothers
tasks.prompt: Which son of Jacob was sold into slavery in Egypt by his own jealous brothers?

normalVariant.prompt: Which son of Jacob was sold into slavery in Egypt by his own jealous brothers?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Joseph, Reuben, or Benjamin?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name Jacob's son who was sold into slavery, and the garment his father had given him.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Joseph, given a coat of many colors
acceptedAnswers: Joseph and a coat of many colors

clues: His father gave him a special multicolored coat.
He later rose to become second in command over all of Egypt.
tasks.teachingReveal: Joseph, given a coat of many colors by his father Jacob, was sold into slavery by his jealous brothers, but God later raised him up as second in command over Egypt.

tasks.title: A Mother's Prayer
tasks.prompt: Who prayed fervently for a son, then gave that son to serve at the tabernacle once he was weaned?

normalVariant.prompt: Who prayed fervently for a son, then gave that son to serve at the tabernacle once he was weaned?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Hannah, Ruth, or Rachel?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the mother, and the son she dedicated to serve under the priest Eli.

clues: The priest Eli at first mistook her silent prayer for drunkenness.
Her son later became a great prophet and judge of Israel.
tasks.teachingReveal: Hannah prayed earnestly for a son, and after God answered with Samuel, she kept her vow to give him to serve at the tabernacle under the priest Eli.

tasks.title: The Governor at the Trial
tasks.prompt: Who was the Roman governor who presided over Jesus' trial and ordered His crucifixion?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was the Roman governor who presided over Jesus' trial and ordered His crucifixion?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Pontius Pilate, Herod, or Caiaphas?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the Roman governor, and the symbolic act he performed to declare himself innocent of Jesus' blood.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Pontius Pilate, who washed his hands
acceptedAnswers: Pontius Pilate and washing his hands

clues: He was the Roman prefect of Judea at the time.
He publicly washed his hands to declare himself innocent of Jesus' blood.
tasks.teachingReveal: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea, presided over Jesus' trial and, despite finding no fault in Him, gave in to the crowd and ordered His crucifixion.

tasks.title: Up in the Tree
tasks.prompt: Which short tax collector climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus over the crowd?

normalVariant.prompt: Which short tax collector climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus over the crowd?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Zacchaeus, Matthew, or Nicodemus?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the tax collector in the tree, and the town where this happened.

clues: He was too short to see over the crowd.
He was the chief tax collector of his town.
tasks.teachingReveal: Zacchaeus, a wealthy but short chief tax collector in Jericho, climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus, who then invited Himself to stay at his house.

tasks.title: Blinded on the Road
tasks.prompt: Who was struck blind by a heavenly light on the road to Damascus and became a great missionary of the early church?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was struck blind by a heavenly light on the road to Damascus and became a great missionary of the early church?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Paul, Peter, or Barnabas?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this missionary, and what he had been doing to the church before his conversion.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Paul, who had been persecuting the church

clues: He was originally traveling to Damascus to arrest followers of Jesus.
He later wrote much of the New Testament.
tasks.teachingReveal: Paul, formerly named Saul and a persecutor of the church, was struck blind by a heavenly light on the road to Damascus and became one of the early church's greatest missionaries.

tasks.title: Baptizing Jesus
tasks.prompt: Who baptized Jesus in the Jordan River?

normalVariant.prompt: Who baptized Jesus in the Jordan River?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it John the Baptist, John the Apostle, or Andrew?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name who baptized Jesus, and what appeared over Jesus afterward, in the shape of a dove.
amplifiedVariant.answer: John the Baptist, when the Spirit of God descended
acceptedAnswers: John the Baptist, the Holy Spirit
John the Baptist and the Spirit like a dove

clues: He lived in the wilderness and ate locusts and wild honey.
He said he was unworthy even to untie Jesus' sandals.
tasks.teachingReveal: John the Baptist baptized Jesus in the Jordan River, and the Spirit of God descended like a dove as a voice from heaven declared Jesus His Son.

tasks.title: From the Tax Booth
tasks.prompt: Which of Jesus' twelve disciples was a tax collector before Jesus called him to follow?

normalVariant.prompt: Which of Jesus' twelve disciples was a tax collector before Jesus called him to follow?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Matthew, James, or Philip?

clues: He was sitting at a tax collector's booth when Jesus called him.
He is traditionally credited with writing the first Gospel.
tasks.teachingReveal: Matthew was a tax collector who left his booth immediately when Jesus called him, becoming one of the twelve disciples and traditionally the author of the first Gospel.

tasks.title: A Queen's Courage
tasks.prompt: Which Jewish queen of Persia risked her own life to save her people from a plot to destroy them?

normalVariant.prompt: Which Jewish queen of Persia risked her own life to save her people from a plot to destroy them?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Esther, Ruth, or Deborah?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the queen, and the official whose plot against her people she exposed.

clues: Her cousin Mordecai raised her and encouraged her to act.
She approached the king uninvited, risking her life.
tasks.teachingReveal: Esther, a Jewish queen of Persia, risked her life by approaching the king uninvited to expose Haman's plot and save her people from destruction.

tasks.title: A New Name
tasks.prompt: Which patriarch wrestled through the night with God and was given the new name Israel?

normalVariant.prompt: Which patriarch wrestled through the night with God and was given the new name Israel?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Jacob, Isaac, or Esau?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the patriarch, and the injury he received during the wrestling match.

clues: He was Isaac's son and Esau's twin brother.
He walked with a limp afterward.
tasks.teachingReveal: Jacob wrestled through the night with God, and though his hip was wrenched, he was blessed and given the new name Israel.

tasks.title: The Walls of Jericho
tasks.prompt: Who led the Israelites into the promised land after Moses' death, and saw the walls of Jericho fall?

normalVariant.prompt: Who led the Israelites into the promised land after Moses' death, and saw the walls of Jericho fall?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Joshua, Caleb, or Aaron?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this leader, and how many days the Israelites marched around Jericho before its walls fell.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Joshua, after seven days of marching

clues: He had been one of the twelve spies sent into Canaan years earlier.
The Israelites marched around the city once a day for six days, then seven times on the seventh.
tasks.teachingReveal: Joshua led Israel into the promised land after Moses' death, and the walls of Jericho fell after the people marched around the city as God commanded, for seven days.

tasks.title: The Only Female Judge
tasks.prompt: Who was the prophetess and judge of Israel who led the people to victory over a Canaanite army?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was the prophetess and judge of Israel who led the people to victory over a Canaanite army?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Deborah, Miriam, or Huldah?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this judge, and the general she called to lead the army into battle alongside her.

clues: She held court under a palm tree, where the people came to her for judgment.
She summoned a general named Barak to lead the army.
tasks.teachingReveal: Deborah, a prophetess and the only female judge recorded in the book of Judges, called the general Barak to lead Israel's army to victory over the Canaanites.

tasks.title: A Fateful Prophecy
tasks.prompt: Which high priest, presiding over the council that condemned Jesus, unknowingly prophesied that one man would die for the nation?

normalVariant.prompt: Which high priest, presiding over the council that condemned Jesus, unknowingly prophesied that one man would die for the nation?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Caiaphas, Annas, or Gamaliel?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this high priest, and his father-in-law, who also questioned Jesus.

clues: He served as high priest that same year.
He argued it was better for one man to die than for the whole nation to perish.
tasks.teachingReveal: Caiaphas, the high priest that year, argued it was better for one man to die for the people — a statement John's Gospel records as an unwitting prophecy of Jesus' death for the nation.

tasks.title: Fire from Heaven
tasks.prompt: On which mountain did the prophet Elijah challenge the prophets of Baal to a contest, calling down fire from heaven?

normalVariant.prompt: On which mountain did the prophet Elijah challenge the prophets of Baal to a contest, calling down fire from heaven?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Mount Carmel, Mount Sinai, or Mount Gilboa?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name the mountain, and the number of prophets of Baal Elijah faced alone.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Mount Carmel, against four hundred fifty prophets

clues: Elijah had the altar soaked with water three times before praying.
Fire fell and consumed the offering, the wood, and even the water.
tasks.teachingReveal: On Mount Carmel, Elijah challenged four hundred fifty prophets of Baal, and God sent fire from heaven to consume his water-soaked offering, proving He alone was God.

tasks.title: Whither Thou Goest
tasks.prompt: What was the name of Ruth's mother-in-law, whom Ruth famously refused to leave, saying 'where you go I will go'?

normalVariant.prompt: What was the name of Ruth's mother-in-law, whom Ruth famously refused to leave, saying 'where you go I will go'?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Naomi, Orpah, or Rahab?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name Ruth's mother-in-law, and the land she and her family had moved to before her husband's death.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Naomi, who had moved to Moab

clues: She had lost her husband and both sons while living in a foreign land.
Ruth was married to one of her sons before his death.
tasks.teachingReveal: Naomi, having lost her husband and sons in Moab, was famously accompanied back to Bethlehem by her loyal daughter-in-law Ruth, who refused to leave her side.

tasks.title: Gifted for the Tabernacle
tasks.prompt: Who was the craftsman specially filled by God's Spirit with skill to lead the building of the tabernacle?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was the craftsman specially filled by God's Spirit with skill to lead the building of the tabernacle?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Bezalel, Aaron, or Hur?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this craftsman, and the tribe of Israel he came from.
amplifiedVariant.answer: Bezalel, from the tribe of Judah

clues: He was named specifically by God to Moses.
He worked in gold, silver, bronze, and skilled craftsmanship.
tasks.teachingReveal: Bezalel, of the tribe of Judah, was filled by God's Spirit with skill and craftsmanship to lead the building of the tabernacle and its furnishings.

tasks.title: A Prophet's Difficult Marriage
tasks.prompt: Which minor prophet was told by God to marry an unfaithful woman, as a living picture of Israel's unfaithfulness to God?

normalVariant.prompt: Which minor prophet was told by God to marry an unfaithful woman, as a living picture of Israel's unfaithfulness to God?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Hosea, Amos, or Joel?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this prophet, and the name of the wife God told him to marry.

clues: His prophetic book uses his own marriage as a picture of God's relationship with Israel.
He prophesied to the northern kingdom of Israel.
tasks.teachingReveal: Hosea was told by God to marry Gomer, an unfaithful woman, as a living illustration of Israel's unfaithfulness and God's persistent love in pursuing His people back.

tasks.title: The First Gentile Household
tasks.prompt: Who was the Roman centurion whose household became the first Gentiles recorded to receive the Holy Spirit, in the book of Acts?

normalVariant.prompt: Who was the Roman centurion whose household became the first Gentiles recorded to receive the Holy Spirit, in the book of Acts?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Cornelius, Felix, or Festus?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this centurion, and the apostle God sent to visit him after a vision.

clues: He was a devout, God-fearing Roman military officer stationed in Caesarea.
He was told in a vision to send for an apostle staying in Joppa.
tasks.teachingReveal: Cornelius, a devout Roman centurion in Caesarea, was visited by Peter after matching visions, and his household became the first Gentiles recorded to receive the Holy Spirit.

tasks.title: A Voice at the Gate
tasks.prompt: What was the name of the servant girl who was so excited to recognize Peter's voice that she forgot to open the gate for him, after his miraculous escape from prison?

normalVariant.prompt: What was the name of the servant girl who was so excited to recognize Peter's voice that she forgot to open the gate for him, after his miraculous escape from prison?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Rhoda, Lydia, or Tabitha?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this servant girl, and whose house she served in, where believers were praying for Peter.

clues: An angel had just freed Peter from prison.
She left him standing outside while she ran to tell the others he was there.
tasks.teachingReveal: Rhoda, a servant girl at the house where believers were praying for Peter's release, was so overjoyed to hear his voice at the gate that she ran to tell the others without letting him in.

tasks.title: A Runaway, Sent Back
tasks.prompt: What was the name of the runaway slave whom Paul sent back to his master with a personal letter, pleading for his forgiveness?

normalVariant.prompt: What was the name of the runaway slave whom Paul sent back to his master with a personal letter, pleading for his forgiveness?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it Onesimus, Timothy, or Titus?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this runaway slave, and the master Paul asked to forgive him.

clues: He had become a believer and useful helper to Paul while Paul was imprisoned.
The short New Testament letter written on his behalf bears his master's name.
tasks.teachingReveal: Onesimus, a runaway slave who became a believer under Paul's ministry, was sent back to his master Philemon with Paul's personal letter pleading for his forgiveness and welcome as a brother.

tasks.title: Counting the Days of Rest
tasks.prompt: According to the creation account, God worked for six days and then rested. Following that same pattern of six days of work, on which day would the rest occur?

normalVariant.prompt: According to the creation account, God worked for six days and then rested. Following that same pattern of six days of work, on which day would the rest occur?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it the seventh day, the sixth day, or the eighth day?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name which day the rest occurred on, and what this pattern is later called as a commanded day of rest.

clues: Count from the first day of work to find the day of rest.
tasks.teachingReveal: The creation account describes six days of work followed by rest on the seventh day. This pattern of a seventh-day rest is later called the Sabbath.

tasks.title: The Road to Rome
tasks.prompt: In New Testament times, what was the name of the major Roman road connecting the port of Brundisium to the city of Rome, used by travelers arriving from the eastern Mediterranean?

normalVariant.prompt: In New Testament times, what was the name of the major Roman road connecting the port of Brundisium to the city of Rome, used by travelers arriving from the eastern Mediterranean?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it the Appian Way, the King's Highway, or the Via Maris?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name this road and the Italian port city it connected to Rome.
amplifiedVariant.answer: The Appian Way, connecting Rome to Brundisium

clues: It was one of the oldest and most strategically important roads of the Roman Republic.
Its name honors the Roman censor who first commissioned it.
tasks.teachingReveal: The Appian Way was a major Roman road linking Rome to the southeastern port of Brundisium, used by travelers arriving from the eastern Mediterranean.
tasks.historicalNote: Widely accepted background: the Appian Way (Via Appia) was one of the earliest and most strategically important roads of the Roman Republic, connecting Rome to the port of Brundisium.

tasks.title: The Parable of the Sower, Retold
tasks.prompt: The host reads this sequence aloud: 'The sower went out to sow. Some seed fell on the path, some on rocky ground, some among thorns, and some on good soil.' How many different types of ground are described in this sequence?

normalVariant.prompt: The host reads this sequence aloud: 'The sower went out to sow. Some seed fell on the path, some on rocky ground, some among thorns, and some on good soil.' How many different types of ground are described in this sequence?

assistedVariant.prompt: Was it four, three, or five?

amplifiedVariant.prompt: Name all the types of ground described in the sequence, in the order given.
amplifiedVariant.answer: The path, rocky ground, thorns, and good soil
acceptedAnswers: Path, rocky ground, thorns, good soil
The path, the rocky ground, the thorns, and the good soil

clues: Count the types of ground named: path, rocky ground, thorns, and one more.
tasks.teachingReveal: The Parable of the Sower describes seed falling on four types of ground: the path, rocky ground, thorns, and good soil — each representing a different response to the message.

tasks.title: A Sound So Sweet
tasks.prompt: Complete this hymn lyric: 'Amazing grace, how sweet the sound, that saved a wretch like ___.'

tasks.title: A Traveler on the Road
tasks.prompt: Your team is traveling and a stranger asks to join you, but you don't know if they can be trusted. What is one wise consideration you would weigh before deciding, and why?
tasks.answer: Any clear, reasoned consideration weighing safety and discernment (for example: ancient roads were safer traveled in company, but Scripture also commends discernment about strangers).
acceptedAnswers: Any clear, reasoned consideration weighing safety and discernment (for example: ancient roads were safer traveled in company, but Scripture also commends discernment about strangers).
tasks.hostGuidance: Judge the reasoning, not the choice. Accept any answer that weighs a real tradeoff — safety in numbers versus trusting an unknown stranger — with a clear reason.

normalVariant.prompt: Your team is traveling and a stranger asks to join you, but you don't know if they can be trusted. What is one wise consideration you would weigh before deciding, and why?

clues: Ancient roads were often unsafe for a lone traveler.
Scripture repeatedly commends hospitality to strangers, but also commends discernment.
tasks.teachingReveal: There is no single right answer here — the goal is reasoned judgment. Ancient travel was often safer in groups, so companionship had real value, but Scripture also commends discernment (Matthew 10:16), so weighing both the value of numbers and the risk of an unknown companion is wise.

tasks.title: Naming the Twelve
tasks.prompt: Name one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.
tasks.answer: Any of the twelve: Peter, Andrew, James son of Zebedee, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot, or Judas Iscariot.
acceptedAnswers: Any of the twelve: Peter, Andrew, James son of Zebedee, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot, or Judas Iscariot.
tasks.hostGuidance: Accept any true, correctly named apostle from the traditional twelve; no repeats from teams that already answered this round.

tasks.teachingReveal: The twelve apostles were Peter, Andrew, James son of Zebedee, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot.
